paras: The Tyro store shooting and somnambulist killing of Uriah Phelps took place in North Carolina in late July or early August 1880, when Phelps, a white storekeeper at Tyro, fired on several Black men during a dispute and was then killed in his sleep by a neighbor hired to guard against their return. Reports differed on whether Phelps's shot struck anyone, and none named the Black men. Papers across the country carried the story as a curiosity of sleepwalking, and the neighbor, O. W. Click, was discharged after a coroner's inquest and preliminary trial.

Phelps kept a store at Tyro, in Davidson County, according to the Charlotte Observer and the Salisbury Democrat, while the Winston Western Sentinel described him as a bar-room keeper in Jerusalem Township, Davie County. The Orangeburg Democrat identified him as "white."

According to the Observer, Phelps and his brother had "a difficulty with some negroes" whom they tried to eject from the store, and a Richmond dispatch said he ejected them. The Western Sentinel reported that in the fracas Phelps "shot at them," not knowing what damage he had done, while the Salisbury Democrat said he shot one man and that "the others swore vengeance against him." No report named the man said to have been shot or described his wounds.

Expecting an attack, Phelps engaged Click, a young neighbor known to walk in his sleep, to stay the night, and the Salisbury Democrat said Phelps's brother Alfred stayed as well. After watching for half the night the men fell asleep, and Click rose and struck Phelps with an axe placed near the bed for defense, nearly or completely severing his head. Click later said he had dreamed that the Black men had entered the store, and the Richmond dispatch said he believed he was "striking one of the negroes."

Click was taken into custody, or by the Salisbury Democrat's account gave himself up. More than a hundred people attended the coroner's inquest and a preliminary trial before Justices Thompson and Hartley, where witnesses for both sides described Click's history of sleepwalking. The justices pronounced the evidence insufficient, and Click returned home. No report of any legal action over Phelps's shooting of the Black men was found.

Only white papers reported the episode, and no coverage in the Black press was found. The Western Sentinel's local item, "Horrible Affair in Davie County," gave the shooting a single clause and called its account the most reliable of "several rumors." The Observer's story, reprinted by the Richmond Dispatch on August 5 under "A Somnambulist's Murder," and a separate Richmond dispatch printed by the New York Sun as "Beheaded by a Somnambulist" spread the case nationally.

Reprints followed in Lancaster, Knoxville, Washington, Wilmington, Delaware, and South Carolina through mid-August, and the Connecticut Western News ran the inquest account on August 28 as "Almost Incredible." Across these versions the Black men appeared only as the unnamed cause of the night watch, and none of the papers said what had become of the man reported shot.

The location differed: the Western Sentinel said Jerusalem Township, Davie County, while the Observer, the Richmond dispatch and the Salisbury Democrat all said Tyro, Davidson County, and the Observer's follow-up carried inquest detail from the scene. Accounts also differed on the shooting itself, from the Observer's silence about any gunfire to the Western Sentinel's "shot at them" and the Salisbury Democrat's "shot one."

reader.title: Tyro store shooting and somnambulist killing of Uriah Phelps
bases: The anti-Black act reported is a single white storekeeper shooting at, or shooting one of, several Black men during a dispute in which he and his brother tried to eject them from his store (A1, A2, A8); no mob, band or officers acted against them, and the coverage centers on Phelps's own killing by Click (A2, A7).

Independent local and regional reports (Western Sentinel A1, Charlotte Observer A2, Richmond dispatch A3, Salisbury Democrat A8) agree that Phelps had a difficulty with several Black men; A1 and A8 both say he fired on them, though they differ on whether anyone was hit.

accounts.label: Western Sentinel (local rumor)
accounts.gist: Phelps, a bar-room keeper in Davie County, had a difficulty with several colored men and shot at them, not knowing the damage done; fearing an attack he asked Click to stay with him.

accounts.label: Charlotte Observer / Richmond dispatch
accounts.gist: Phelps and his brother tried to eject some Black men from the store at Tyro, Davidson County; no shooting is mentioned; Phelps engaged Click to watch for their return.

accounts.label: Salisbury Democrat
accounts.gist: Phelps shot one of the Black men on a Saturday; the others swore vengeance, and his brother Alfred and Click stayed the night with him.

accounts.label: Click's statement at the inquest
accounts.gist: Click said he dreamed the Black men had entered the store and that a bloody fight followed; he woke fleeing down the stairs.

framing.detail: The local Western Sentinel headed it 'Horrible Affair in Davie County' and gave the shooting in one clause, centering on Click's beheading of Phelps.

The Observer and Richmond versions ran nationally as a sleepwalking oddity ('A Somnambulist's Murder', 'Beheaded by a Somnambulist', 'Almost Incredible.'), mentioning the Black men only as the expected attackers.

conflicts.note: The Western Sentinel said it gave 'the most reliable' of several rumors; the Observer, the Richmond dispatch and the Salisbury Democrat all say Tyro, Davidson County, and the Observer's follow-up adds inquest detail, so Davidson is better supported.

info: The Salisbury Democrat dated the shooting 'last Saturday' (its issue date is not given; A8 ran Aug. 12); A1 (Aug. 5) said the killing of Phelps came 'a few nights since'; the Richmond dispatch of Aug. 4 placed the killing on the night of Aug. 3-4.
Phelps's store at Tyro, Davidson County (A2, A3, A8); the Western Sentinel placed it in Jerusalem Township, Davie County (A1).
Several unnamed Black men ('several colored men' A1, 'some negroes' A2, A8); none is named in any report.
Phelps, a white storekeeper/bar-room keeper (Uriah Phelps A2, A3; U. M. Phelps A8; 'white' A10); his brother joined in trying to eject the men (A2).
